chunk_map.heading: A signal that can only say yes is not a test

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L4: "He asks for the third line" (L10) closest; 'He' resolves to Barry O'Reilly named L4, 'the third line' to the bulleted template L6-8; 'this capability/outcome/signal' are the template's fill-in slots, not referents.
grep for 'lecture|module|earlier|previous|opening' in body L1-12 -> 0 pointers at another file; only sequential in-file reference is L10 'the third line'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'the X you did/saw/caught' in body; closest L12 'agree on it before the agents start building' is a forward instruction, not a recalled beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal or demo beat; plain exposition

rules_evaluated.evidence: L4-12 carry a self-standing claim: a bet needs a signal that could come back no (L4), with template, example and ask.
L1 'A signal that can only say yes is not a test' vs L4 'needs a signal that could come back no' and L12 'could embarrass you': content supports the header, no contradiction.

Per-chunk sub-items: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'; no anaphora triple (L6-8 are template slots, not repeated openers); no superlative; no number+retraction (L10 '5 percent... 48 hours' is a labelled attributed example); no abstraction-noun stack; no verb triplet. Closest: L10 'a number and a window' (concrete, two legs).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep compendium|firing|forcing function|beat|mood|surface in body -> 0. Closest L4 'bet' is ordinary product vocabulary, used in the header's sense and defined in-line as a hypothesis.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L6-8: three bold spans ('We believe', 'will result in', 'We will have confidence to proceed when'). They are the fixed slot names of O'Reilly's template (checklist item names, one per line, a handle per item as the law/consolidation allowance reads), and the maintainer fidelity guard pins the third span's wording, so the 7-word span is the quoted template phrase, not a bolded lead sentence. No bold in narrative L4, L10, L12. Harm (every bullet opens with a bolded sentence, monoculture) absent: spans are slot labels, bullet payloads are plain.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: slide file; presence in the composed deck is decided by the host lecture's include line, not this body

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1 'A signal that can only say yes is not a test' is a claim, the lecture-heading form; slide is a lecture-type law slide where the header is the teaching.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L12 'Write a signal that could embarrass you, and agree on it before the agents start building.' overlaps L4 'a signal that could come back no' and L10 'before anything is built', but adds the move (draft an embarrassing signal, agree it up front) and is not a koan restating the header: it is an imperative. Bullets L6-8 are the template, each a slot the room fills.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
